But it might come as a surprise to some that many of her stories were inspired by a country house in Cheadle, Greater Manchester. Abney Hall is the subject of a new episode of Hidden Manchester on BBC Sounds after the Cheadle Civic Society erected an information board in the grounds explaining the novelist's connections. In 1902, Christie first arrived at Abney Hall when she was about 11 years old as her older sister Madge lived at the house after marrying into the wealthy Watts family. Nestled in the village of Cheadle, the gothic building has high-ceilinged rooms, gold chandeliers and a red velvet carpet running down the centre of a large wooden staircase. Outside, there are crosses etched into the stone walls as well as distinctive chimney stacks - no doubt the inspiration for one of her stories The Secret of Chimneys. Image source, Cheadle Civic Society Image caption, Abney Hall and the surrounding gardens forms part of a new heritage trail Trever Evers, from the society, said there were plenty of features to inspire the writer. "You know Abney Hall had it all, it had a waterfall, it had a tunnel under the drive," he said. "She loved the fact that the house had back passageways and staircases that they used to hide from each other." Evers added that the geography of Abney Hall was itself an inspiration. The Northern Ireland-born comedian, real name James Joseph Mulgrew, died on 3 August aged 80. Among the veteran comedians attending his funeral were Catchphrase host Roy Walker, Crackerjack presenter Stu Francis, Freddie "Parrot face" Davies and Syd Little, half of comedy act Little and Large. Image caption, Two of Jimmy Cricket's daughters, Jamie, 46 and Katie, 41 The star's daughter Katie, who is also a stand-up comic, explained the bow-tie request. "I made a joke and said, 'shall we wear bow ties?' and now my mum is even wearing part of his stage costume," she said. Katie added: "We are heartbroken but he was pure joy and we just wanted to tip our bow ties to him." title: Man denies charge over Manchester synagogue attack

evidence_packet.title: Man denies charge over Manchester synagogue attack
evidence_packet.lead: Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, 49, denied failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity
evidence_packet.summary: Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim, 49, denied failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Man denies charge over Manchester synagogue attack - BBC News Image source, PA Media Image caption, The charges are linked to the 2 October 2025 attack By Paul Burnell North West Published 21 August 2026 A man has denied failing to disclose information in relation to the Manchester synagogue attack. Hekmat Omar Ali Hakim appeared before Westminster Magistrates' Court and pleaded not guilty to failing to disclose information regarding terrorist activity. The 49-year-old, of St James Road in Higher Broughton, Salford, spoke only to confirm his name and indicate his plea. He was remanded into custody to appear at at the Old Bailey on 25 September. Worshippers Melvin Cravitz and Adrian Daulby were killed when Jihad Al-Shamie, 35, a Syrian-born British citizen, drove into the gates of the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue on 2 October. He then began attacking with a knife, while wearing a fake suicide belt, before being shot dead by police outside the synagogue. First direct charge Sally-Anne Russell, prosecuting, alleged CCTV evidence of conversations between Hakim and Al-Shamie show him "condoning and supporting" the terrorist action. Hakim attended the same mosque as Al-Shamie and travelled in a car with him on various occasions before the attack, which took place on Yom Kippur, one of the holiest day of the Jewish religious calender Cravitz, 66, died from knife wounds inflicted by Al-Shamie while Daulby, 53, was struck by a single gunshot wound to the chest fired by an armed police officer scrambled to the scene in the Crumpsall area of the city. Three other men were treated in hospital for serious injuries. Greater Manchester Police said there have so far been eight arrests in connection with the attack, however this is the first charge that "relates directly".

evidence_packet.summary: Damian Woolfenden is accused of posting video footage of a terrorist attacker online
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A teenager accused of stirring up racial hatred against Jewish people and foreigners and sharing a video of a mass killing online has appeared in court Damian Woolfenden, 18, is accused of posting Christchurch attacker Brenton Tarrant's live-streamed video of the 2019 killings on to the self-described "pro-white" platform White Pilled TV Woolfenden, formerly of Bury, Greater Manchester, also allegedly posted the manifesto of far-right terrorist Andres Breivik, who killed 77 people in two attacks in Norway on June 22 2011, on to a Telegram group, the court heard He appeared at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Friday via video link, and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth Woolfenden has been remanded in custody and will next appear at the Old Bailey on 25 September He is said to have had on his home computer the manifesto of US white supremacist mass shooter Payton Gendron and German neo-Nazi synagogue shooter Stephan Balliet along with a firearms guide

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A paramedic has been struck off for telling a woman suffering a stroke to stop acting "like a baby" and accused them of lying about their pain The Healthcare Professionals Tribunal Service heard Rachel Claire Lemonofides made "inappropriate and degrading" comments heard on a 999 call at the woman's home in 2024 It found Lemonofides was guilty of racially motivated discrimination on the grounds of ethnicity and breached professional boundaries The patient underwent emergency surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital, Manchester, and was diagnosed with a brain bleed and abdominal aortic aneurysm. North West Ambulance Service said all patients were "entitled to be treated with dignity and respect" The service added: "There is no place within our organisation for colleagues who do not uphold those values." Police are investigating after the Believe Achieve CIC project in Stoneclough, Bolton, was targeted on Monday night. The bike hub was being built after reports of young people in the area using illegal motorised bikes - and the group aims to give youngsters access to bicycles while teaching road safety and maintenance skills. Tunde Olasupo, project founder, says the site was "stormed" by people who vandalised a surrounding fence and forcibly opened a container that will house the hub. They added there had been opposition to the project, with concerns about further antisocial behaviour. There were also concerns about its location and environmental impact, Olasupo said. 'Upset' "Of course, I'm upset, and when you see something that you've worked hard for deliberately damaged, you're human, it hurts," he told BBC Radio Manchester. He said the site had been targeted before. "The objective is to balance access and community benefit with protecting and enhancing the natural environment, and that's one of the things that we're trying to make very clear to people." V News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:16, 22 Aug 2026 In his darkest of times Tony Wilson was still capable of a good quote. He was fighting for his life after developing renal cancer when he delivered a memorable quip Doctors had suggested he take Sutent. It would not provide a cure but would extend his life. But Manchester Primary Care Trust refused to fund the £3,500 per month cost of the drug. Yet patients alongside him at The Christie Hospital and living in Cheshire did receive funding Music industry and media friends rallied to help pay. Branding the situation a scandal Wilson pointed out that tummy tucks were available on the NHS, and said at the time: " I thought where am I going to find the money? I'm the one person in this industry who famously has never m He never paid for private health care because he was a socialist. Wilson died on August 10th 2007 aged 57 after the cancer progressed and he suffered a heart attack On his Peter Saville designed headstone in Manchester's Southern Cemetery it says: "Broadcaster Cultural Catalyst". His part in Manchester's renaissance from post-industrial gloom was huge

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford 'I can't sleep because I hear them scurrying and writhing in the walls' Christine Smith, 74, says scratching sounds keep her awake every night, but despite doctors urging for her to be rehoused, her housing association claims there is no activ News Charlotte Hall Local Democracy Reporter 07:38, 22 Aug 2026 Every night, Christine Smith dreads going to bed The 74-year-old has lived in the same social housing in Little Hulton for 40 years, and in that time has spent thousands to turn the place into a real home. But for the past two years, it’s felt like anything but That’s because almost every night since early 2024, she’s heard ‘scratching and scraping’ inside her walls, she says. Behind the wallpapers and galleries of family photos, she’s convinced rats have the run of the home’s infrastructure Her housing association, ForHousing, says they’ve found ‘no evidence’ of rats during a number of call-outs in the last few years. The LDRS has heard recordings of the sounds taken by Christine and her neighbours in July, along with footage of the rats caught just outside their ho View 3 Images Christine Smith says the lack of sleep is affecting her health. The 24-year-old was reported missing by her grandmother on February 2, 2022 She was one of the people Alisha was closest to in her young life, with the pair having spent a period of time living together. But she had not heard from Alisha in a couple of weeks and was growing concerned about her Greater Manchester Police issued a public missing person's appeal to try and find Alisha on March 1, 2022. Later that month, the search became a murder investigation, as detectives came to the sad conclusion Alisha had 'come to serious harm' I spoke to Alisha's grandmother outside her Ashton-under-Lyne home in the days following GMP's announcement. She was in shock at the events that were unfolding around her and clearly worried sick about her beloved granddaughter She was also determined to do what she could to try and bring her beloved granddaughter home. She was keen to speak to the Manchester Evening News as part of this, but at the moment we spoke she was expecting a GMP officer to arrive any minute with an update about Alisha

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tony Wilson Even after we lost him Tony Wilson remains a catalyst for debate Peter Hook wants a £250,000 bronze tribute, but as Neal Keeling writes, turning an avant-garde disruptor into a static sculpture has sparked a fierce row across the Irwell. V News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:16, 22 Aug 2026 In his darkest of times Tony Wilson was still capable of a good quote. He was fighting for his life after developing renal cancer when he delivered a memorable quip Doctors had suggested he take Sutent. It would not provide a cure but would extend his life. But Manchester Primary Care Trust refused to fund the £3,500 per month cost of the drug. Yet patients alongside him at The Christie Hospital and living in Cheshire did receive funding Music industry and media friends rallied to help pay. Branding the situation a scandal Wilson pointed out that tummy tucks were available on the NHS, and said at the time: " I thought where am I going to find the money? I'm the one person in this industry who famously has never m He never paid for private health care because he was a socialist. Wilson died on August 10th 2007 aged 57 after the cancer progressed and he suffered a heart attack On his Peter Saville designed headstone in Manchester's Southern Cemetery it says: "Broadcaster Cultural Catalyst". His part in Manchester's renaissance from post-industrial gloom was huge

title: Seven foot statue of Tony Wilson planned on Salford riverbank

evidence_packet.title: Seven foot statue of Tony Wilson planned on Salford riverbank
evidence_packet.lead: Tony Wilson Seven foot statue of Tony Wilson planned on Salford riverbank Joy Division star Peter Hook reveals plans for a crowd-funded bronze tribute in Greengate Square depicting 'Mr Manchester' gazing across the Irwell.
evidence_packet.summary: Tony Wilson Seven foot statue of Tony Wilson planned on Salford riverbank Joy Division star Peter Hook reveals plans for a crowd-funded bronze tribute in Greengate Square depicting 'Mr Manchester' gazing across the Irwell. Neal Keeling reports
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tony Wilson Seven foot statue of Tony Wilson planned on Salford riverbank Joy Division star Peter Hook reveals plans for a crowd-funded bronze tribute in Greengate Square depicting 'Mr Manchester' gazing across the Irwell. Neal Keeling reports. View 6 News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 22 Aug 2026 His swagger as a cultural pioneer earned him the title of Mr Manchester. But a seven-foot tribute to him could soon rise in Salford Anthony H Wilson, the gifted, influential journalist and music mogul left his mark on Manchester. But he was a proud Salfordian He was born in the city and before studying at Jesus College Cambridge he attended De La Salle Grammar School in Salford. His parents, Sydney and Doris ran a tobacconist shop on Regent Road. As a small child he lived with his parents in a flat above the shop Wilson's maternal family, the Knupfers, had jewellers and watchmaker shops on the same road It has been convincingly argued that the success of Madchester music scene and his Hacienda nightclub was a root cause of the city being able to emerge from post-industrial decline

evidence_packet.summary: Bury Police officer denies PC's claim he described her braided hair as 'like a mop' A misconduct hearing involving seven serving officers and two former officers in Bury is continuing News Paul Britton Reporter 21:05, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bury Polic A police officer facing an a
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Police officer denies PC's claim he described her braided hair as 'like a mop' A misconduct hearing involving seven serving officers and two former officers in Bury is continuing News Paul Britton Reporter 21:05, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bury Polic A police officer facing an allegation he described a female PC colleague's braided hair as 'looking like a mop' told a misconduct hearing she's lying. PC Mohammed Abid said the complainant - a black African-born constable referred to as PC Y - had 'made up' claims that he often s Giving evidence he said he had 'absolutely not' made the comment. "I didn't refer to her hair as a mop," he told the hearing on Friday Opening the case on Monday, Counsel for GMP, Steven Reed, said PC Y wore her hair in braids and it was in braids at the time the comment at the centre of the complaint was made Mr Reed said PC Abid denied making any comment towards her at all, the hearing was told, and claimed he had been the 'victim of racism' A group of Bury-based officers deny breaches of standards in relation to complaints made by the PC, including the mocking and mimicking of her African accent

evidence_packet.lead: Crime Cocky Thailand ‘couriers’ paid extra baggage charges to bring 22 suitcases filled with £13m of cannabis into UK 'My man gonna be on the other side - don't leave the airport until you see him leave' News Paul Britton Reporter 17:27, 21 Aug 2026 V A gang of drug smugglers - i
evidence_packet.summary: Crime Cocky Thailand ‘couriers’ paid extra baggage charges to bring 22 suitcases filled with £13m of cannabis into UK 'My man gonna be on the other side - don't leave the airport until you see him leave' News Paul Britton Reporter 17:27, 21 Aug 2026 V A gang of drug smugglers - i
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Cocky Thailand ‘couriers’ paid extra baggage charges to bring 22 suitcases filled with £13m of cannabis into UK 'My man gonna be on the other side - don't leave the airport until you see him leave' News Paul Britton Reporter 17:27, 21 Aug 2026 V A gang of drug smugglers - including three from Greater Manchester - paid extra baggage charges as they tried to bring 22 suitcases packed with cannabis from Thailand into the UK because they were so heavy Police said the couriers were part of a plot to smuggle cannabis worth £13.8m into the country. A court heard they each had two suitcases packed with 20 kilos of cannabis The couriers even had to pay an excess charge at Bangkok Airport to put them in the hold because of their weight, the National Crime Agency said as all 11 people were convicted Bradley Lloyd, 27, of no fixed abode but from Wythenshawe ; Lewis Ross, 35, of Rupert Street, Bolton and Claire McCullough, 36, of Meliden Crescent, Wythenshawe, all pleaded guilty to a charge of knowingly being concerned in the carrying of cannabis with intent to evade prohibiti The three - together with eight others convicted - will be sentenced at a later date

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Money Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business After being told her feet looked like a SpongeBob cartoon character, Jennifer Bailey turned her painful bunions into a £1.8m fashion brand loved by celebrities. View 5 Images Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 17:11, 21 Aug 2026 A mum who received abuse from online trolls about her foot condition now brings in millions every year with her shoe business. Jennifer Bailey, 48, uses social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok to promote her Jennifer grew up in Wigan but now lives in Newton-le-Willows with her husband and two daughters, aged 11 and 13. It was during her own teenage years that she developed bunions - hard, bony bumps that form on the inside of the foot at the base of the big toe However, the painful condition also inspired her to start her own business when she was made redundant from her job as Head of Marketing at the Science and Engineering faculty at Salford University "I needed to figure out what I was going to do next because I'd found out I was pregnant at the same time with my youngest daughter," Jennifer told the M.E.N "I had to think about what my next steps were going to be. Was I going to go and get another job with a pregnant belly, or was I going to wait until after I've had the baby and then figure it out?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Woman, 20, denies committing arson at Dovestone Reservoir Shania Care-Slede appeared via videolink at a hearing at Minshull Street Crown Court News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 15:53, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Shania Care-Slede, 20 (Image: Instag A young woman accused of setting off fireworks near Dovestone Reservoir shortly before a huge wildfire broke out on the moors has denied charges she faces Shania Care-Slede, 20, appeared via videolink at a hearing at Minshull Street Crown Court on Friday (August 21) to enter pleas to three counts She has been charged with arson; arson being reckless as to whether life is endangered (aggravated arson); and dangerous driving Ms Care-Slede, wearing a white top and black blazer, appeared on screen. She pleaded guilty to dangerous driving. She pleaded not guilty to the two arson charges The particulars of the first charge are that on on July 11, 2026 she committed aggravated arson ‘destroying by fire moorland belonging to United Utilities’, being reckless as to whether the life of others was endangered

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely redevelop Bury’s transport interchange could also see new homes built Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has unveiled its ambition to create scores of new homes on land between the interchange and Bury Market. It is now looking for a partner to help it bring its vision to life The scheme could see between 70 and 80 apartments built across an up to six-storey block. While TfGM initially advertised the scheme as fully affordable in its procurement notice, it has now said it is ‘tenure agnostic’ The Local Democracy Reporting Service understands affordable homes are still expected to be the best option for the site, but TfGM is open to a wider range of bids for the contract The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said. Whoever wins the contract would be expected to take responsibility for arranging funding for the scheme, which could include securing grant funding

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 13 hours ago Jimmy Cricket funeral RECAP from Salford Cathedral as iconic comedian laid to rest The much-loved comic was known for his bowler hat and his 'and there's more' catchphrase An order of service for the funer The much-loved performer, born James Mulgrew, died on August 3 at the age of 80 following a short illness. Originally from Cookstown in Northern Ireland, he had made Rochdale his adopted home in the later years of his life Known for his signature bowler hat, wellington boots and the catchphrase 'and there's more', Cricket became a TV staple in the 80s. In tributes following his passing, Roy Walker described him as a 'sincere wee fella', whilst Christopher Biggins described Cricket as 'unbelievable In a statement, Cricket's family said the artist, who was a devout Catholic, was their 'greatest champion' and that he 'loved us all loudly'. Youngest son, a former comedian who became a priest, Father Frankie Mulgrew said the comic had asked for the last rites twice, “almost lik A popular face on television and on the stage, Cricket was given his own show in 1985, named after his iconic catchphrase And There's More. The show ran for four series. He also had a BBC Radio 2 show called Jimmy's Cricket Team, and also regularly made pantomime appearances In 2007, he was one of the comedy icons to appear in the music video for Peter Kay and Matt Lucas' Comic Relief cover of The Proclaimers' hit I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)

title: Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move

evidence_packet.title: Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two G
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two G
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two Greater Manchester towns could be reinstated. The move, being considered by Lancashire councils , would see the previous 236 route brought back into use It would start in the Lancashire town of Rawtenstall and run through to Bolton , stopping off in Ramsbottom along the way. If signed off, the service would begin at the end of November. It would be expected to run every two hours on Mondays through to Saturdays The move to restore the 236 has been welcomed by residents in Ramsbottom, who say they will also benefit from the new connection into Bolton. Currently, those travelling between the two towns have to change buses in Bury One resident said it was ‘great news’, adding they ‘hope it actually happens’ A second person said: “Hopefully this will happen. It's ridiculous that at the moment if you live in the Holcombe Brook area of Ramsbottom you can only go to Bury. With this you can go to Bolton and Rawtenstall.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside Tributes pour in for 'beautiful soul' killed in Woodhead Pass crash 'Amazing' Jean Higginbottom tragically died at the scene News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 09:49, 21 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Jean Higginbottom tragically died in the crash Heartfelt tributes have flooded in for a 'lovely' former postal worker and animal lover who was tragically killed in a crash near Woodhead Pass . Jean Higginbottom has been named as the 73-year-old woman killed in a crash on Manchester Road, near Tintwistle , on Wednesday (August Derbyshire Police says Jean, from Hyde , was driving her silver Renault Clio along Manchester Road when a Nissan Pixo collided with her car close to Millbrook House at 2.30pm that day. Paramedics and police rushed to Jean's aid, but she was sadly pronounced dead at the scene Since Jean was named as the crash victim on Thursday, tributes have poured in on the Manchester Evening News ' Facebook page, from people who knew and loved her. Bea, of Art by Bea Creations in Glossop, posted: "My lovely Godmother, truly one of a kind lady will be missed by many Taz Mass wrote: "Jean was a jolly, kind and caring lady. We always competed against each other with her piebald pony Marie and my piebald cob Murphy, many years ago at New Barn shows. She has been to my house a couple of times too. Not seen her in a number of years but do have fo Rose Elizabeth said: "She was [a] truly amazing person inside and out and a force to be reckoned with! I’m absolutely heartbroken. Rest in peace Jean until we meet again, wait for me with a glass of pinot."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Boohoo Fashion firm Boohoo fined huge sum by watchdog over misleading pricing practices An investigation took place in France Comments News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 08:17, 21 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Boohoo (Image: PA) Fast fashion firm Boohoo has been fined 2.3 million Euros - around £2 million - by the French consumer watchdog over misleading pricing practices The Directorate-General for Competition, Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control (DGCCRF) said Boohoo, part of the recently rebranded Debenhams Group, had given shoppers a false impression about the discounts being offered on the French version of its website Manchester-based Boohoo did not take account of previously applied promotions, or even increased prices before applying a discount, according to the DGCCRF It found 95 per cent of the listings analysed failed to comply with its rules, with 40 per cent offering no price reduction, 7 per cent offering a smaller discount than advertised and 48 per cent actually increasing prices Boohoo also used terms that are banned, such as 'leather' or 'suede' to describe synthetic products, going against French rules on clothes and footwear labelling

V News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:16, 22 Aug 2026 In his darkest of times Tony Wilson was still capable of a good quote. He was fighting for his life after developing renal cancer when he delivered a memorable quip Doctors had suggested he take Sutent. It would not provide a cure but would extend his life. But Manchester Primary Care Trust refused to fund the £3,500 per month cost of the drug. Yet patients alongside him at The Christie Hospital and living in Cheshire did receive funding Music industry and media friends rallied to help pay. Branding the situation a scandal Wilson pointed out that tummy tucks were available on the NHS, and said at the time: " I thought where am I going to find the money? I'm the one person in this industry who famously has never m He never paid for private health care because he was a socialist. Wilson died on August 10th 2007 aged 57 after the cancer progressed and he suffered a heart attack On his Peter Saville designed headstone in Manchester's Southern Cemetery it says: "Broadcaster Cultural Catalyst". His part in Manchester's renaissance from post-industrial gloom was huge

Neal Keeling reports. View 6 News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 07:12, 22 Aug 2026 His swagger as a cultural pioneer earned him the title of Mr Manchester. But a seven-foot tribute to him could soon rise in Salford Anthony H Wilson, the gifted, influential journalist and music mogul left his mark on Manchester. But he was a proud Salfordian He was born in the city and before studying at Jesus College Cambridge he attended De La Salle Grammar School in Salford. His parents, Sydney and Doris ran a tobacconist shop on Regent Road. As a small child he lived with his parents in a flat above the shop Wilson's maternal family, the Knupfers, had jewellers and watchmaker shops on the same road It has been convincingly argued that the success of Madchester music scene and his Hacienda nightclub was a root cause of the city being able to emerge from post-industrial decline

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford LIVE EVENT ENDED Updated 13 hours ago Jimmy Cricket funeral RECAP from Salford Cathedral as iconic comedian laid to rest The much-loved comic was known for his bowler hat and his 'and there's more' catchphrase An order of service for the funer The much-loved performer, born James Mulgrew, died on August 3 at the age of 80 following a short illness. Originally from Cookstown in Northern Ireland, he had made Rochdale his adopted home in the later years of his life Known for his signature bowler hat, wellington boots and the catchphrase 'and there's more', Cricket became a TV staple in the 80s. In tributes following his passing, Roy Walker described him as a 'sincere wee fella', whilst Christopher Biggins described Cricket as 'unbelievable In a statement, Cricket's family said the artist, who was a devout Catholic, was their 'greatest champion' and that he 'loved us all loudly'. The show ran for four series. He also had a BBC Radio 2 show called Jimmy's Cricket Team, and also regularly made pantomime appearances In 2007, he was one of the comedy icons to appear in the music video for Peter Kay and Matt Lucas' Comic Relief cover of The Proclaimers' hit I'm Gonna Be (500 Miles)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Cocky Thailand ‘couriers’ paid extra baggage charges to bring 22 suitcases filled with £13m of cannabis into UK 'My man gonna be on the other side - don't leave the airport until you see him leave' News Paul Britton Reporter 17:27, 21 Aug 2026 V A gang of drug smugglers - including three from Greater Manchester - paid extra baggage charges as they tried to bring 22 suitcases packed with cannabis from Thailand into the UK because they were so heavy Police said the couriers were part of a plot to smuggle cannabis worth £13.8m into the country. A court heard they each had two suitcases packed with 20 kilos of cannabis The couriers even had to pay an excess charge at Bangkok Airport to put them in the hold because of their weight, the National Crime Agency said as all 11 people were convicted Bradley Lloyd, 27, of no fixed abode but from Wythenshawe ; Lewis Ross, 35, of Rupert Street, Bolton and Claire McCullough, 36, of Meliden Crescent, Wythenshawe, all pleaded guilty to a charge of knowingly being concerned in the carrying of cannabis with intent to evade prohibiti The three - together with eight others convicted - will be sentenced at a later date

title: Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business

evidence_packet.title: Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business
evidence_packet.lead: Money Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business After being told her feet looked like a SpongeBob cartoon character, Jennifer Bailey turned her painful bunions into a £1.8m fashion brand loved by celebrities.
evidence_packet.summary: Money Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business After being told her feet looked like a SpongeBob cartoon character, Jennifer Bailey turned her painful bunions into a £1.8m fashion brand loved by celebrities. View 5 Images Comments News Lee Grimsditch
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Money Wigan mum abused by online trolls now runs million pound shoe business After being told her feet looked like a SpongeBob cartoon character, Jennifer Bailey turned her painful bunions into a £1.8m fashion brand loved by celebrities. View 5 Images Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 17:11, 21 Aug 2026 A mum who received abuse from online trolls about her foot condition now brings in millions every year with her shoe business. Jennifer Bailey, 48, uses social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok to promote her Jennifer grew up in Wigan but now lives in Newton-le-Willows with her husband and two daughters, aged 11 and 13. It was during her own teenage years that she developed bunions - hard, bony bumps that form on the inside of the foot at the base of the big toe However, the painful condition also inspired her to start her own business when she was made redundant from her job as Head of Marketing at the Science and Engineering faculty at Salford University "I needed to figure out what I was going to do next because I'd found out I was pregnant at the same time with my youngest daughter," Jennifer told the M.E.N "I had to think about what my next steps were going to be. Was I going to go and get another job with a pregnant belly, or was I going to wait until after I've had the baby and then figure it out?

evidence_packet.lead: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely re
evidence_packet.summary: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely re
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury New homes planned at Bury Interchange as part of major redevelopment The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said Comments News Hannah Richardson 14:15, 21 Aug 2026 Updated 15: Major plans to completely redevelop Bury’s transport interchange could also see new homes built Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) has unveiled its ambition to create scores of new homes on land between the interchange and Bury Market. It is now looking for a partner to help it bring its vision to life The scheme could see between 70 and 80 apartments built across an up to six-storey block. While TfGM initially advertised the scheme as fully affordable in its procurement notice, it has now said it is ‘tenure agnostic’ The Local Democracy Reporting Service understands affordable homes are still expected to be the best option for the site, but TfGM is open to a wider range of bids for the contract The project would ‘support Bury council’s wider regeneration and housing plans for the town centre’, TfGM has said. Whoever wins the contract would be expected to take responsibility for arranging funding for the scheme, which could include securing grant funding

title: Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move

evidence_packet.title: Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move
evidence_packet.lead: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two G
evidence_packet.summary: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two G
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Ramsbottom and Bolton's historic 236 bus route could be restored as residents hail move It could begins as soon as November Comments News Hannah Richardson 10:40, 21 Aug 2026 View Image Bolton Interchange (Image: Manchester Evening News) A former bus route connecting two Greater Manchester towns could be reinstated. The move, being considered by Lancashire councils , would see the previous 236 route brought back into use It would start in the Lancashire town of Rawtenstall and run through to Bolton , stopping off in Ramsbottom along the way. If signed off, the service would begin at the end of November. It would be expected to run every two hours on Mondays through to Saturdays The move to restore the 236 has been welcomed by residents in Ramsbottom, who say they will also benefit from the new connection into Bolton. Currently, those travelling between the two towns have to change buses in Bury One resident said it was ‘great news’, adding they ‘hope it actually happens’ A second person said: “Hopefully this will happen. It's ridiculous that at the moment if you live in the Holcombe Brook area of Ramsbottom you can only go to Bury. With this you can go to Bolton and Rawtenstall.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Tameside Tributes pour in for 'beautiful soul' killed in Woodhead Pass crash 'Amazing' Jean Higginbottom tragically died at the scene News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 09:49, 21 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Jean Higginbottom tragically died in the crash Heartfelt tributes have flooded in for a 'lovely' former postal worker and animal lover who was tragically killed in a crash near Woodhead Pass . Jean Higginbottom has been named as the 73-year-old woman killed in a crash on Manchester Road, near Tintwistle , on Wednesday (August Derbyshire Police says Jean, from Hyde , was driving her silver Renault Clio along Manchester Road when a Nissan Pixo collided with her car close to Millbrook House at 2.30pm that day. Paramedics and police rushed to Jean's aid, but she was sadly pronounced dead at the scene Since Jean was named as the crash victim on Thursday, tributes have poured in on the Manchester Evening News ' Facebook page, from people who knew and loved her. Bea, of Art by Bea Creations in Glossop, posted: "My lovely Godmother, truly one of a kind lady will be missed by many Taz Mass wrote: "Jean was a jolly, kind and caring lady. We always competed against each other with her piebald pony Marie and my piebald cob Murphy, many years ago at New Barn shows. She has been to my house a couple of times too. Not seen her in a number of years but do have fo Rose Elizabeth said: "She was [a] truly amazing person inside and out and a force to be reckoned with! I’m absolutely heartbroken. Rest in peace Jean until we meet again, wait for me with a glass of pinot."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Every new trader in the city reaches the same fork eventually. Two boxes on a registrar’s page, one ending .co.uk, one ending .com, both available, both costing roughly the price of a round. The choice looks cosmetic, and it gets treated that way It is the one decision in building a business website that follows you everywhere afterwards: invoices, email signatures, van livery, the card in the window. Changing it later means redirects, reprinted stationery and a few uneasy months while search engines work out which addres Most owners settle it on availability, and if the name is taken on .com and free on .co.uk, that is usually that. Registrars bundle the domain with hosting and a small business website builder , so the extension gets picked in the same five minutes as the template and the colour Google is unusually direct about this. Its own documentation lists country-code domains as a strong signal that a site is intended for a particular country, notes that server location then stops mattering, and puts the catch in the same table: a country domain can only target one For a Manchester small business selling to people who can drive to the door, that ceiling is the point of the thing rather than a restriction on it. A .co.uk address tells a search engine, and a customer scanning results on a phone at a bus stop, that this is a British operation The constraint bites later, if at all. A trader who picks up wholesale customers in Rotterdam, or starts posting orders to Dublin, finds the same signal now working against the traffic they want, and no setting anywhere undoes it

There were balloons, flowers, cards and a cake made by the home’s head chef Mary, 98, from Gateshead, and Peter, 97, from Newark, met at the Oxford Galleries dance hall in Newcastle and married at St Chad’s Church in Gateshead. evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email A blue plaque has been unveiled at a Bowdon house to mark the life of William Wood, the social reformer known as “The Climbing Boys’ Friend” The plaque is at Willow Cottage, 28 Stamford Road, where Wood lived after retiring there in 1847. It was unveiled last week at a ceremony organised by Trafford Council’s Local Studies team, attended by residents, historians, council members, Connor Rand MP and the Friends of Bowd Wood, born in 1782, was a wool merchant who began campaigning in 1826 after seeing a young boy fall to his death inside a chimney onto a live fire. “Climbing boys” were children sent up chimneys to sweep them, often suffering burns, respiratory illness, deformity and suffocation From Bowdon he funded prosecutions against master sweeps who broke child labour laws, put up placards at railway stations and wrote to newspapers He also challenged magistrates and even Queen Victoria over the use of a child sweep at Windsor Castle His work with Lord Shaftesbury included testimony to the House of Lords in 1853, which helped lead to the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875. Wood died in 1868, aged 85, seven years before the practice was banned. Six chimney sweeps from five towns carried his coffin to St Mary’s Churc

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Northern Care Alliance (NCA), which runs four hospitals in Greater Manchester, including Salford Royal Hospital, was put under an NHS enforcement notice to improve patient safety, in June But whistle blowers have now told an investigation by the Independent and Channel 4 that they were discouraged from reporting concerns The trust has told the BBC it is working to address staff concerns and has "clear processes to investigate incidents" A spokesperson for NCA said the trust changed the way it was organised in response to demands by NHS England to improve standards in surgical wards, tackling backlogs in spinal and gynaecology services But the investigation found patients are alleged to have been "left dying or in pain" in overcrowded A&E corridors, before then receiving invasive treatments which might have been avoided if there was no delay, the investigation claims Other allegations raised in the report include staff suggesting their accounts of serious harm or death are "shut down or not investigated properly"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Care Quality Commission (CQC) inspection report published today (Wednesday 5 August) has found that Manchester City Council’s adult social care services are Good The CQC’s local authority assessment for Manchester, the first of its kind under a new system, scored the Council’s services at 72% - making it the highest rating for any of the England’s biggest cities outside London Adult social care provides support to citizens ranging from young adults to people who are in the later years of their lives. Adult social care works with vulnerable adults who have physical, learning disabilities, and mental health needs Last year (2025/26) 9,937 people received long-term adult social care support, which includes support in people’s own homes, as well as support to people in Care Homes, Extra Care schemes and supported living. Another 6,232 were accessing short-term care through services such as Strengths highlighted in the CQC report include timely assessments for most people, with the starting point of all assessments being what is important to the individual and what they want to achieve. Effective early support was also praised as well as good access to support (most The assessment also identified some areas for development, which the Council will be prioritising as part of wider continuous improvement and transformation plans. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The £35 million project set within 154 acres has transformed the former site of Worsley New Hall, restoring the historic walled garden, lake and surviving buildings Originally built for the 1st Earl of Ellesmere between 1840 and 1845, Worsley New Hall was a grand Gothic-style mansion, complete with glorious, formal landscaped gardens It’s now one of UK’s must-see gardens with so much to enjoy for visitors of all ages Step inside the magnificent 11-acre Weston Walled Garden, the site’s jewel in the crown. One of the largest Victorian walled gardens in the UK, it showcases a range of growing techniques and edible plants There’s also the spectacular Paradise Garden showcasing exotic planting inspired by Asiatic and Mediterranean gardens. The orchard and nearby bee and butterfly garden, have been designed to attract wildlife The Peel Learning Garden, supported by The Peel Group, will help schoolchildren learn how plants affect our lives and the planet, whilst the Community Wellbeing Garden provides a space for people to garden, socialise and relax

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Totally Stockport has launched a new masterplan as part of its Going Green programme, setting out a bold and practical vision for a greener, healthier and more vibrant town centre Developed by Layer.studio in consultation with retailers and residents, ‘Going Green’ focuses on the places people use every day and sets out a strategy, toolkit and initial projects to support regeneration, wellbeing and economic activity With the aim to create a connected, people-focused green infrastructure network, streets, squares and key routes have been reviewed to create a one connected green network The masterplan spans the 80Ha Totally Stockport BID Boundary and combines quick wins with longer-term visions in key areas, setting out a practical route to a town centre that’s even more walkable, attractive and economically active Paul Kelsall, BID Director at Totally Stockport and co-owner of Stockport based Kelsall Architects, said: “At its core, ‘Going Green’ is about joining the green dots “From Merseyway to the Underbanks and Chestergate, the masterplan shows how simple, well-placed changes such as more planting and enhanced greenery can change the face of the town centre

It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Our Mayor is now our Prime Minister, and the skills agenda he's brought to Downing Street is one we've lived and breathed for over a decade Andy Burnham has spent some of his first fortnight in office setting out plans to reshape technical education and get more young people into work, built on the MBacc model developed here in Greater Manchester. This is familiar ground for us. For over ten years Manchester Digital That gap has become harder to bridge, economic uncertainty, higher costs and cautious hiring are playing their part as is AI, which is starting to strip out the routine tasks junior roles were built on. This has resulted in the entry-level jobs young people used to start in being Alan Milburn's interim review, published in May, put a shortage of entry-level jobs at the centre of a "generational fault line", with one in eight young people now not in education, employment or training. His recommendations come in the autumn, but the direction is already clea We sit right in the middle of this, we represent the employers in this sector so we hear it from both sides, everyone knows that the talent pipeline is crucial to whether the sector thrives but it's harder to do in practice than it sounds. evidence_packet.summary: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Дронотур Бумбокса Європою. Листопад-грудень 2026 року. Презентація максі-синглу "Живий" Кожного разу, коли перед менеджментом гурту Бумбокс стоїть завдання написати пресреліз, ми починаємо згадувати цікаві факти. Скільки концертів зіграли, скільки грошей зібрали, які пісні видали. Це база. Непогано ще пам’ятати, чи був гурт у країні, до якої ми збираємося, чи це пер О, як би хотілося написати: "Концерт гурту Бумбокс" — і як у Львові за добу продано 8000 квитків. Так-так, ми не про Львів розповідаємо, хоча теж про Європу Наші віддані слухачі, якщо ви перебуваєте за кордоном, сподіваємось, вам буде цікаво дізнатися, що після традиційної перерви на декілька місяців, Бумбокс поїде в турне від Ізраїлю до Німеччини, від Англії до Польщі, від Ірландії до Словаччини та Чехії І повеземо ми в це турне свіженький, як херсонський кавун, максі-сингл “Живий”, підсилений піснями з різних альбомів, під частину яких виросли ви, а під частину зростають ваші діти Тож ознайомтеся, будь ласка, уважно з розкладом туру, купуйте квитки заздалегідь, готуйте гроші на донати та мерч — зустрінемося в листопаді
